metrics.result:
The 15-second landscape teaser is rendered at `./out/film.mp4` (1920x1080, 30 fps, 450 frames, silent). I checked a contact sheet of the frames, and lint came back clean at 16:9 and 9:16. I didn't play back the rendered MP4 itself.

- **0–4s:** "Nordlicht" rises on navy #0B1F3A. A soft teal #4FD1C5 aurora glow drifts underneath, and a teal underline wipes in.
- **4–7.5s:** "Plan less." in white, with a slow push-in.
- **7.5–11s:** "Live more." in teal, with the glow swelling behind it.
- **11–15s:** the Nordlicht wordmark, then "Coming March 2027" in teal.

The only copy is your name, tagline and date. It has no music or voice-over, because I wasn't given a track. The script is at `./film.reel` if you want to change timing or text.

checklist.item: uses navy #0B1F3A and teal #4FD1C5 as the main colours
checklist.evidence: Navy background throughout with teal glow, 'Live more.' and 'Coming March 2027' in teal.
Large bold white 'Nordlicht' in the opening and end frames.
'Plan less.' then 'Live more.' on separate full-frame cards.
Final frames 11.9–14.4s show Nordlicht with teal 'Coming March 2027' beneath.

checklist.item: looks like a polished product teaser, not a slideshow
checklist.evidence: Four text-only cards on a gradient with no product visuals or graphic elements; it reads as a title-card slideshow.

problems: There is no product imagery, UI, icon or logo mark. It is only text on a gradient, so it doesn't show what Nordlicht is and feels like a slideshow of title cards.
The glow is a soft blurry blob and doesn't evoke an aurora, which the name suggests. It is barely visible on some frames, so the background feels flat and empty.
The scenes are separate static cards with only a slow scale and a rise-in. There is little motion variety or energy, and the pacing is slow for a teaser.

The hierarchy is flat. The tagline is split across two cards, and the end card repeats the same title with a small date. The thin teal bar in the opening scene is a weak accent and disappears after the opening.
The 'Coming March 2027' line is small compared with the title and sits close to it. The end card has a lot of empty space and no call to action.
judge.verdict: The video is clean, legible and on brand, and it has all the requested copy in the right order. It is generic: four text cards on a blurred gradient with no visual concept or product cue. It is acceptable but not a polished teaser, and the user would probably ask for more visual interest.
